name: Orkla India Ltd
title: Orkla India Ltd - 544595 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q2 FY27 revenue up 18.4% on ~20% spice price increases, volume only 2.9%, and EBITDA margin down ~100bp to 15.9%; growth is price-led, not a supply-side signal.

summary.headline: Orkla India Q2 FY27 revenue grew 18.4% to INR776 crore (19.4% on revenue from operations) with volume up 2.9%; EBITDA margin 15.9%, down ~100 bps YoY.
summary.overview: Revenue growth accelerated versus Q1, led by spice price increases of about 20% to offset sharp commodity inflation, with volume growth of 2.9%, the highest of the last three quarters. EBITDA rose 12.6% to INR124 crore, but margin moderated about 100 bps YoY as pricing lagged input costs and Project Bolt and PLI effects weighed. Management said underlying EBITDA growth was 11.6% excluding PLI and Project Bolt investments, and H1 underlying margin was 17.2%. Kerala distribution restructuring and Project Bolt (quick commerce) are showing early results, with digital commerce rising to 10% of domestic revenue.

segments.name: Spices
segments.commentary: Revenue +25.1% YoY, largely price-led (pricing ~20%+), with positive volume but moderated by inflation and Kerala restructuring. Chilli and coriander drove the inflation. Spices grew about 48% YoY in value per the appendix, per management.

segments.name: Convenience foods
segments.commentary: Revenue +7.7% YoY against a high base because festive season shifted into Q3 (Dussehra and Diwali). Sequential growth continued; volume growth moderated.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Revenue +20% YoY, with Eastern leading growth; volumes grew despite price inflation and festive timing shift.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue +11.7% YoY; GCC +22.7% YoY, described as the key growth engine.

segments.name: Digital commerce
segments.commentary: Share of domestic business rose from 8.9% in Q1 FY27 to 10% in Q2 FY27; rest-of-India digital commerce revenue +33.6% YoY.

guidance_outlook: Management aspires to grow well beyond 10-12% revenue growth; if commodity inflation moderates to 5-7%, it sees potential for 8-10% volume growth.
Pricing actions taken late in Q2 are expected to flow through with full benefit in Q3, which should aid margins.
Standalone modern trade restructuring about 50% complete; remainder to finish by December 2026.
Kerala spices distribution rollout to continue through March 2027, starting with Kasaragod and Kannur.
Project Bolt is entering its final quarter of implementation; festive sweets and meals platforms to be tested through Q3.
capex_capacity: Kerala convenience foods distribution separation completed in June 2026; effective coverage up about 10% (1.1x) and sales productivity up 1.27x vs Q4 FY26 levels.
Wet batter (MTR Minute Fresh) launched in Hyderabad about 3 months ago, with 5-7% market share; Bangalore was the only prior market. Next large cities to follow after Hyderabad stabilises.
Project Bolt present in about 240 towns across rest of India; focus on top 28 cities; consumer reach has tripled through social content.
Around 15 new sweets launches for the festive season via digital commerce; 38 launches in H1 (23 in Q1, 15 in Q2).
Management did not disclose capex amounts or capacity figures in the call.
demand_pricing: Spice price increases of over 20% taken to pass through commodity inflation; pure spices priced at roughly 10% over raw commodity wholesale price; blended spices on a more calibrated approach.
Spice volumes slightly moderated due to price elasticity; company does not disclose volume by category or geography.
Spice prices stabilised after crop cycle ended and stock moved to cold storage; a speculative spike in late September triggered another price increase.
Organised share of South Indian spice market about 40% (up from 30-35% over five years), with 60% unorganised.
Quick commerce: dry batter has very little competition (dominant); wet batter No. 2 brand; sweets segment highly competitive (Haldiram and others); meals segment fragmented.
Digital commerce mix is margin accretive at gross margin level because of higher convenience food share.

qa_highlights.question: How is EBITDA calculated, given the presentation EBITDA of ~12.5% differs from operating profit measures?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA excludes finance costs, forex losses and fair value losses on financial instruments (reported in other expenses), exceptional items and depreciation; an explanatory note was provided.

qa_highlights.question: Volume growth detail for spices and convenience foods?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not give category volume numbers; both categories had positive volume, with spices volume moderated by 20%+ pricing and convenience foods moderated by the festive shift into Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Price breakdown for blended vs pure spices, drivers of the 48% spice increase, and current price trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Pure spices track commodity moves directly; blended spices priced more calibrated. Chilli and coriander drove the inflation. Prices now largely stable after crop cycle ended, with one speculative spike in late September.

qa_highlights.question: Kerala distribution restructuring status, volume and share impact, and H2 milestones?
qa_highlights.answer: Convenience food separation completed June 2026; standalone modern trade about 50% done, to finish by December 2026; spice coverage expansion just started in Kasaragod and Kannur. Standalone modern trade volume +16% QoQ; Kerala spice volume returned positive in Q2 due to Onam.

qa_highlights.question: Wet batter scaling and Project Bolt competition in rest of India?
qa_highlights.answer: Wet batter now in Hyderabad (3 months) with 5-7% share, to stabilise before next large cities. Project Bolt covers about 240 towns; quick commerce is the main lever; competition differs by segment.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term volume vs price contribution and pricing power?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aspires to grow beyond 10-12%; if inflation moderates to 5-7%, possible 8-10% volume growth. Believes category can take 2-3% price increases given spices are only 2.5-3% of consumer spend.

qa_highlights.question: Margin glide path, especially at Eastern, and impact of restructuring?
qa_highlights.answer: Eastern mix is about 50% pure spices, 45% blended spices and the balance convenience foods; plan is to build convenience foods to lift margins, alongside consolidated manufacturing and digitisation efficiency programmes. No numeric margin target given.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation in chilli and coriander; margin compression (EBITDA margin down ~100 bps YoY) if pricing lags costs.
Volume elasticity from 20%+ spice price increases; volume growth only 2.9% in Q2.
Speculative spice price movements, as seen in late September.
Kerala restructuring and Project Bolt investments weighing on EBITDA growth (ex-PLI and Bolt, growth 11.6%).
Competitive intensity in sweets and meals segments in quick commerce; wet batter No. 2 position.
Reliance on PLI benefits in PAT; other income from surplus cash supporting profit.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line momentum and strategic projects, but candid that margins moderated and volumes slowed under price pressure. Management was open on EBITDA definitions and Kerala progress, but was less specific on category volumes and gave no numeric margin target.
key_quotes: The revenues have grown by about 18.4% in Q2, and volume growth is improving.
We continue to deliver double-digit EBITDA growth while maintaining a healthy level of profitability through this inflationary cycle.
We believe this reflects a healthy and resilient underlying margin performance.

growth.why: Management aspires to grow beyond 10-12% revenue growth (second consecutive double-digit quarter), backed mainly by ~20% spice price increases and Hyderabad wet batter/digital expansion, with no capacity additions or capex disclosed and volume growth only 2.9%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Late-Q2 price actions flow through fully in Q3, but EBITDA margin fell ~100 bps YoY to 15.9% and H1 adjusted margin was ~40 bps down at 17.2%, with no numeric margin target given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No capex amounts or capacity figures disclosed; the Kerala separation and Hyderabad wet batter are distribution and market launches, not new plant or line capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 volume grew only 2.3% and Q2 2.9% under 20%+ spice price hikes, with management saying 8-10% volume is possible only if commodity inflation eases to 5-7%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed and no utilisation figure was given, so no read on a new capex announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held its double-digit growth aspiration but gave no raised numeric guidance, and volume growth is only 2.9% in Q2.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: EBITDA margin fell ~100 bps YoY to 15.9% as pricing lagged chilli and coriander inflation, and volume elasticity to 20%+ spice price rises is a stated risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: About 15 festive sweets launches are planned via digital commerce (38 launches in H1), and Project Bolt meals and sweets platforms are to be tested through Q3.

rows.label: Wet batter scale-up beyond Hyderabad
rows.why: Wet batter launched in Hyderabad about 3 months ago at 5-7% share; next large cities follow only after Hyderabad stabilises.

rows.label: Standalone modern trade restructuring completion
rows.why: About 50% complete with modern trade volume up 16% QoQ; remainder guided to finish by December 2026.

rows.label: Kerala spices distribution rollout
rows.why: Spice coverage expansion just started in Kasaragod and Kannur, with rollout guided to continue through March 2027.

tone.note: Management was confident on top-line momentum, Kerala restructuring and Project Bolt, but candid that margins moderated and volumes slowed under price pressure; analysts pressed on EBITDA definitions and category volumes, and management gave no numeric margin target.
